papers.title: Correlative mapping links extracellular matrix architecture to local mechanics in cardiac aging
papers.abstract: Cardiac aging is accompanied by extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, but how changes in matrix architecture relate to local tissue mechanics remains poorly understood. Here, we quantified six image-derived architectural descriptors across selected ECM components in young and aged murine myocardium and integrated them into an architectural index that we term 'ArchI'. Age-associated architectural changes differed among ECM components, with higher ArchI values observed for fibrillar collagen, fibronectin, and laminin-associated networks. To examine how defined structural changes affect the component descriptors, we developed controlled synthetic geometries and a stochastic network model. These analyses revealed index sensitivity to matrix occupancy, fiber width, and network continuity. We then combined nanoindentation of fresh cardiac tissue slices with subsequent immunofluorescence staining and imaging of collagen to correlate local tissue stiffness with ECM architecture in corresponding regions. Aged myocardium exhibited higher ArchI and Young's modulus, with local heterogeneity in their spatial correspondence. Age-adjusted regression revealed a positive association between ArchI and Young's modulus, with a steeper association in aged myocardium. Together, these findings reveal component-specific ECM remodeling during aging and provide a means to examine spatial structure-mechanics relationships in the aging heart.

papers.title: Beyond screens: a gaze-driven auditory human-computer interface
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces enable humans to communicate and manipulate external devices by converting physiological signals into actions. These signals often have a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) too low to enable their use in real-world Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). Notably, electrooculography (EOG) measurements of gaze direction exhibit a higher SNR, making them widely employed in HCI applications with displays. Nevertheless, display-free paradigms can also leverage the high SNR of EOG measurements of eye gaze. Current auditory paradigms present options sequentially, extending stimulus presentation time and reducing the information transfer rates (ITRs) compared to visual displays. This paper introduces an HCI approach that combines the SNR of eye gaze with a rapid auditory display paradigm. This paradigm leverages the human capacity to focus on a single auditory stream presented among others. By integrating eye gaze with a rapid auditory display, our method attains average accuracies of 82.7% for a five-option menu and average peak ITRs of 41 bits/min. This increase in performance represents a stride towards practical HCIs in real-world scenarios and display-free smart devices.

papers.title: Biophysics-informed generative models improve activity and thermostability of designed ribozymes
papers.abstract: Generative models of biological sequences can produce molecules that fold and function similarly to natural ones. A further challenge is to steer generation toward a desired property, such as resistance to high temperature. This is particularly difficult when available sequence data are limited, and typically requires probing thousands of variants experimentally, either through directed evolution or to retrain a model specialized to the targeted property. Ideally, however, one would avoid such an expensive experimental step. Here, we show that biophysical information can complement limited evolutionary data to guide the design of catalytic RNA molecules toward increased activity and thermostability. We combine a sequence generative model with a physical score based on the Turner nearest-neighbor model, whose parameters were originally derived from calorimetric measurements, independently of the sequence family considered. On its own, this physical score is ineffective for design: optimizing it destroys function, likely because it is blind to the catalytic core and to tertiary contacts. However, when coupled to the generative model, it provides complementary information that enables better designs than evolutionary data alone. We demonstrate this on self-splicing group I intron ribozymes: starting from designs that are active at 37 C but inactive at 60 C, fewer than ten substitutions are sufficient to confer catalytic activity at 60 C.

papers.title: Engineering Bacteriophages to Overcome Complement-Mediated Neutralization
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages) are promising alternatives to antibiotics for treating antibiotic-resistant infections, but their clinical durability is limited by the host immune response against phages. Using phage T4 as a model and both C1q-KO and C3-deficient mice, we show that antibody recognition of phages triggers complement-dependent neutralization and clearance of phage particles in vivo. To mitigate this complement-mediated clearance, we engineer phages to display the complement-modulating Factor H binding peptide, a phage we call T4-FactorH.BP. Indeed, T4-FactorH.BP resists inactivation in human donor sera from individuals with pre-existing antibodies against T4 phage. Similarly, in mice immunized against T4 circulation of T4-FactorH.BP is prolonged in vivo. These results establish a critical role for the classical complement pathway in phage clearance and provide a path towards improving the pharmacokinetics of phage therapeutics in vivo by evading complement.

papers.title: Rigid granular scaffolds reveal transcriptional responses to cellular confinement
papers.abstract: A large variety of cells migrate through confined spaces in vivo, where mechanical confinement influences their fate and function. However, existing in vitro confinement models are low-throughput, limiting discovery of confinement-responsive genes and recovery of confined cells. Here, we present non-annealed glass microparticle scaffolds (GlaMS) as a scalable, high-throughput 3D confinement system with interconnected voids that mimic physiological confinement while enabling efficient cell retrieval. Using LOVAMAP, a computational tool that segments void spaces to estimate spatial constrictions, we quantified confinement levels in GlaMS and compared them with ex vivo interstitial spaces to identify the sphere size that best mimics in vivo confinement. Using human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) as a mechanosensitive cell model, confinement within GlaMS was found to induce morphological changes, accelerated migration, altered YAP signaling, and enhanced osteogenic priming after replating, demonstrating transient confinement-induced effects. Taking advantage of the high throughput capabilities of GlaMS, we performed RNAseq on populations of confined cells and identified confinement degree-dependent shifts in gene expression. TMEM158 emerged as a previously unrecognized confinement-sensitive gene, was independently validated in microchannel assays, and was found by loss-of-function analysis to contribute to efficient confined migration. Together, this work establishes GlaMS as a scalable platform for population-level confinement mechanobiology, allowing recovery and molecular profiling of cells exposed to predictable three-dimensional confinement.

papers.title: Multifunctional CNT-based Platform for Enhanced Dopaminergic Differentiation and Electrochemical Dopamine Sensing from Human iPSC-derived Neurons.
papers.abstract: Pairing neuro-electrochemical sensors with physiologically relevant neuronal models represents a new frontier in the study of neurodegenerative diseases. In this work, we reported an electroactive platform for in situ detection of dopamine, combining human iPSC-derived neurons with carbon nanotubes. In this system, carbon nanotubes served a triple role: enhancing the electroactive area, catalyzing dopamine oxidation, and promoting subtype-specific dopaminergic differentiation. We developed a robust protocol achieving functional dopaminergic neurons, confirmed via qPCR, immunocytochemistry, MEA electrophysiology, and calcium imaging. CNT substrates were associated with a significant increase in the TH/neurofilament overlap (37.90 {+/-} 3.80% vs. 26.01 {+/-} 3.75% in controls). Applying differential pulse voltammetry and chronoamperometry, we quantified extracellular dopamine at 1.25 M and confirmed the stimulus-dependent release induced by benztropine and KCl depolarization. Post-electrochemical immunostaining confirmed that neurons retained their morphology and TH expression. Overall, this work establishes a novel framework for neurodegenerative disease modeling that recapitulates key electrophysiological and neurochemical features of dopaminergic neurons, representing a powerful tool for disease modeling, drug screening, and the development of next-generation neuro-biosensors.

papers.title: Reproducible and open-source statistical shape models of the pose-normalized adult lower body: development and comparative evaluation
papers.abstract: Accurate skeletal geometry is important for subject-specific musculoskeletal modeling, but the choice of statistical representation may affect anatomical reconstruction. This study developed a reproducible workflow and compared four statistical shape model families of the pose-normalized adult lower body: pooled global, articulated shape-pose, sex-conditioned shared-basis, and independently fitted sex-specific models. Models were developed from computed-tomography-derived geometries of 20 adults and evaluated using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Model coefficients were estimated from each held-out subjects complete registered surfaces, assessing dense-surface representational generalization. Outcomes included model compactness, whole-body and bone-wise surface root-mean-square errors, and reconstruction errors for hip, knee, and ankle joint centers. A pelvis-referenced bounding-box anisotropic-scaling baseline was included as a geometric comparator. The pooled global and sex-conditioned models shared a principal-component basis and therefore identical compactness spectra, with the first component explaining 90.16% of the variance. These models provided the most consistent reconstruction performance. The articulated model had ankle and knee joint-center errors 9.1 and 5.4 mm higher, respectively, than the pooled global model. Independently fitted sex-specific models did not improve whole-body reconstruction over the pooled global or sex-conditioned models in this small cohort. Under the present evaluation, the pooled global and sex-conditioned models reduced whole-body surface errors by approximately 4.1 and 4.0 mm, respectively, relative to scaling. The pooled global model also reduced ankle and knee joint-center errors by 12.5 and 11.0 mm. These results characterize the implemented representations within the available dataset. The scaling comparison was not input matched, and sparse-input and external validation remain necessary. The accompanying LowerBodySSM workflow and interactive Companion provide a reproducible resource for further anatomical modeling and evaluation.

papers.title: Synthesis of Plasma Membrane-Enriched Nanodiscs from Giant Plasma Membrane Vesicles
papers.abstract: Nanodiscs are highly versatile biomaterials with applications in cell membrane mimicry, membrane protein (MP) characterization, and hybrid biological-abiological material synthesis. The plasma membrane (PM) is an ideal starting material for nanodisc synthesis because it naturally houses a diverse array of functionally important MPs in their native lipid environment. However, the PM comprises a small fraction of the total membrane material in a typical eukaryotic cell. Traditional methods to isolate the PM suffer from undefined relative PM enrichment compared to other cellular membranous structures. Here, we introduce a method to synthesize PM-enriched nanodiscs (PMNDs) from giant plasma membrane vesicles (GPMVs). We show that GPMV-derived PMNDs retain functional membrane-anchored protein, exhibit uniform size and morphology, and bind specifically and dose-dependently to the PM of cells expressing a cognate receptor. This strategy offers broad applicability for synthesizing nanodiscs with novel MPs for investigating PM-nanomaterial interactions, cellular targeting, and vaccine development using immunologic MPs.

papers.title: EEG Source Localization with High-Resolution 40-Tissue Head Models: A Comparative Study with MEG during Photic Driving
papers.abstract: While MEG source localization pipelines often employ head models of one single compartment with homogeneous conductivity, researchers and clinicians use at least 3 different layers in head models for EEG source localization. Recent AI-based segmentation makes it possible to generate individualized head models with 40 high-resolution, non-nested tissues. We present a pipeline that can make use of, and test, these highly realistic models for EEG source localization: with the boundary element fast multipole method (BEM-FMM), we compute transcranial electric stimulation (TES) solutions on the full 40-tissue geometry and use them reciprocally to obtain the EEG leadfields. Out approach runs on a single modest workstation, requiring approximately 4.5 min per EEG channel for a mesh of about one million elements at a relative residual of 1e-4. We applied the pipeline to six participants undergoing intermittent photic stimulation at half their individual alpha peak frequency, comparing 61-channel EEG source localizations from 40-tissue and 5-layer models with each other and with localizations from simultaneously recorded MEG. We further compared noiseless synthetic EEG topographies of the two models across the entire cortex. The two models produced highly consistent EEG source localizations (weighed relative difference below 3%), both in close agreement with the MEG localizations within the visual cortex. The synthetic topographies also agreed closely, with differences scaling approximately linearly with the angle between the source orientations of the two models, underscoring the importance of accurate source normals in fixed-orientation source models. These results establish 40-tissue models as a practical and robust basis for EEG source localization, and open the way to applications where nested geometries cannot represent the anatomy, such as infants or patients with skull defects, injuries, or tumors.

papers.title: Internalizing-peptide engineering converts blocking anti-EGFR antibodies into EGFR lysosomal targeting degraders
papers.abstract: Conventional antibodies targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) primarily inhibit receptor activation rather than efficiently eliminating the receptor from tumor cells. Here, we investigated whether engineering full-length anti-EGFR antibodies with internalizing peptides could promote receptor degradation, enhance their biological activity and enable the development of recombinant receptor-depleting antibodies. Chemical conjugation of cetuximab (CTX) to the polyarginine peptide R12 enhanced intracellular uptake, reduced surface-accessible EGFR and decreased total receptor abundance in vitro. CTX-R12 conjugate also enhanced inhibition of wound repopulation in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cell lines, an effect reproduced using the R12 variant LINC18, and transferred to the independent blocking anti-EGFR antibody LEI. Incorporation of LINC19, a variant of LINC18, into recombinant full-length antibody fusion proteins preserved their activity. The LEI-LINC19 fusion (LEIP), reduced surface-accessible and total EGFR, with bafilomycin A1 reversing receptor loss and supporting an acidification-dependent endolysosomal component of degradation. Functional studies indicated that the antibody-peptide reduced DNA synthesis rate. Furthermore, siRNA-mediated EGFR depletion increased TKI-associated reductions in cellular biomass in PC9 cells and increased gefitinib responsiveness in H1975 cells. Consistently, combining LEIP with either osimertinib or gefitinib produced greater inhibition of H1975 wound repopulation than the corresponding individual treatments. LDH analysis revealed increased membrane-damage-associated LDH release following LEIP-gefitinib treatment but no additional increase with LEIP-osimertinib relative to osimertinib alone. These effects extended to 3D NSCLC models. CTX-R12 inhibited PC9 3D colony development, whereas LEIP restricted expansion of established PC9 colonies and reduced the projected area of H1975 spheroids. In H1975 spheroids initiated with 1,000 or 5,000 cells per well, LEIP-containing combinations with osimertinib or gefitinib produced greater inhibition of the spheroid size than the corresponding TKI-only treatments. Nuclear Green DCS1 staining revealed no detectable baseline core necrosis in untreated H1975 spheroids, whereas LEIP treatment was associated with DNA-positive material within and surrounding the spheroids. Moreover, LEIP-treated H1975 spheroids exhibited markedly reduced EGFR immunofluorescence compared with control and parental LEI-treated spheroids. Together, these findings demonstrate that internalizing-peptide engineering of blocking anti- EGFR antibodies can generate full-length EGFR-depleting fusion proteins with enhanced biological activity. The recombinant LEIP format and its activity in 3D in vitro NSCLC tumor models support further investigation of fusion antibody-mediated EGFR degradation as a complementary strategy to EGFR kinase inhibition.

papers.title: Myosin II-FAK-paxillin Signaling Governs Mechanosensitive Responses of Neuronal Cells to Magnetic Stimulation
papers.abstract: Recent work has highlighted transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) as a promising, non-invasive therapeutic approach for a variety of diseases such as Parkinsons disease (PD). Magnetic stimulation (MS) causes action potentials that result in dopamine release and increases in neuroplasticity. While secretion and the electrophysiology of MS have been well characterized, other downstream effects of MS are unknown. Here we characterize a mechanotransduction pathway that is activated in response to MS in a dopaminergic cell line (N27-A). Integrin tension was measured using DNA-based integrin tension sensors (ITSs), and cytoskeletal and focal adhesion structure was quantified in response to pharmacological inhibitors and activators of common mechanotransduction pathways. MS enhances ITS rupture in N27-A cells in a dose dependent manner. Additionally, both pulse frequency and number control ITS rupture. The ITS rupture that MS causes occurs through both cell migration-independent and -dependent mechanisms. Furthermore, MS enhances integrin forces in N27-A cells through a myosin II- and FAK-dependent pathway by creating more internal adhesions with increased phosphorylated paxillin. This work definitively demonstrates that MS can cause robust changes in mechanotransduction, which likely regulate neuroplasticity and provide an addition mechanism to explain the efficacy and potential of TMS therapy.

papers.title: Interspecies differences in lamina cribrosa fiber composition and architecture might arise from differences in optic nerve head size and mechanical constraints
papers.abstract: The lamina cribrosa (LC) is a complex network of fibers that plays an important mechanical role in protecting optic nerve axons as they exit the eye. Both the architecture and composition of the LC network varies throughout animal species. However, the function of these differences between species is unknown. We hypothesize that this variety in LC architecture and composition is a result of species-specific adaptations to the mechanical constraints present in each species' optic nerve head. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel optimization framework to systematically derive optimal LC fiber architecture and composition under different mechanical constraints. We then compared predicted LC architectures to instant polarized light microscopy images of actual human, tree shrew, monkey, cow, pig, and rat LCs. Distinct features from the various LCs were replicated by varying the mechanical constraints, consistent with our hypothesis. The wheel-and-spoke architecture of the tree shrew LC was captured with angularly symmetric loading conditions. Non-radial fibers like those found in monkey and human LCs were captured by adding horizontal eye rotation tractions. The softer glial LC of the rat and stiffer collagenous LC of larger species were replicated by a two-material extension of the model. To our knowledge, these are the first results that systematically show how interspecies differences in LC architecture and composition can arise from mechanical constraints and size. This work can result in better interpretation of animal models and provide a point of comparison for changes in LC architecture under pathological conditions such as glaucoma.

papers.title: CorridorKit: Open-source software for geometric comparison of skull base surgical corridors
papers.abstract: CorridorKit is open-source research software for comparing rigid surgical access corridors in physical image coordinates. Its Python engine represents finite instruments, circular portals, target samples, and protected geometry, and keeps evaluated paths linked to their reached samples, insertion depths, and clearance states through command-line, desktop, and 3D Slicer interfaces. In a reproducible 413-sample phantom, two portals reached 94 and 267 samples, with 326 in their union. Numerical verification included 82 analytical angular comparisons and 4,720 voxel-distance queries. In a public sellar CT example, conditional target coverage rose from 0 to 533 of 536 voxels as the modeled sphenoidotomy opening radius increased from 4 to 8 mm.

papers.title: Mass Transfer Formulations Shape Oxygen Transport and Tissue Oxygenation in Microvascular Networks
papers.abstract: Continuous oxygen delivery is essential for cerebral tissue function, yet its local supply characteristics remain incompletely understood. Quantifying oxygen transport in microvascular networks (MVNs) requires a physiologically consistent description of oxygen exchange between vascular compartments via mass transfer coefficients (MTCs). We investigate how different MTC formulations influence oxygen availability and hypoxic burden in realistic MVNs, and whether they produce relevant local differences in tissue oxygenation. A multicompartment oxygen transport model describing exchange between red blood cells (RBCs), plasma, and tissue in realistic MVNs was developed and evaluated against in vivo measurements. Three RBC-plasma MTC formulations were compared: constant, hematocrit-dependent, and hematocrit- and saturation-dependent. Additionally, a double-flux formulation incorporating a direct RBC-to-tissue flux was compared with standard single-flux formulations. Global tissue oxygen distributions were comparable across RBC-plasma MTC formulations, but hematocrit- and saturation-dependent MTC formulations predicted larger hypoxic tissue fractions. The largest differences occurred under low hematocrit, with local plasma oxygen partial pressure PO2 differing by {approx}6 mmHg along representative vascular paths. Introducing the direct RBC-tissue exchange reduced tissue PO2 at low hematocrit and enhanced it at high hematocrit, with the largest differences observed in small vessels. Sensitivity analysis revealed that RBC oxygen diffusivity can alter the double-flux effect magnitude. MTC assumptions substantially influence predicted oxygen availability and hypoxic burden, particularly under low-hematocrit conditions and in small vessels, underlining the need for their accurate definition. The proposed model provides a basis for evaluating these effects, improving the interpretation of oxygen transport predictions in realistic MVNs.

papers.title: A midnight snack for spirulina: a dual-substrate kinetic model for second cheese whey supplementation of Arthrospira platensis
papers.abstract: Arthrospira platensis (Spirulina) is a widely used strategic cyanobacterium whose cultivation cost remains a primary barrier to large-scale production. Mixotrophic growth on dairy by-products offers a simultaneous route to increase biomass concentration and valorize industrial waste streams. Here, we investigate the effect of Parmigiano Reggiano second cheese whey supplementation on A. platensis batch cultivation under continuous and alternating photoperiods. Whey supplementation increased final biomass in a dose-dependent manner under both continuous and alternating light. At the higher supplementation level, cultures under alternating light reached the same final biomass as under continuous illumination within the cultivation window. To interpret the interaction between whey availability, photoperiod, and biomass accumulation, we developed a kinetic model in which inorganic substrate assimilation is light-dependent, while whey-associated growth can contribute during both light and dark phases through a phenomenological dark-phase coefficient. Model and experimental results are consistent with the assumption that photoperiod mainly modulates the rate of biomass accumulation rather than the attainable biomass, under sufficient substrate availability. These results support a nutrient-stoichiometric interpretation of the biomass ceiling and suggest that second cheese whey supplementation can reduce dependence on continuous artificial lighting, providing a promising route for more resource-efficient Arthrospira cultivation.

papers.title: Modeling Aerobic-Anaerobic Microbial Electrolysis Cells for Multi-step Methane Conversion
papers.abstract: The bioconversion of methane by anaerobic methanotrophs has a higher carbon and energy efficiency compared to aerobic processes, suggesting significant potential for producing value-added chemicals and reducing green-house-gas emissions. However, their practical use still faces many challenges regarding their culturing, genetic manipulation, and integration into multi-species consortia. Here we mathematically model a microbial electrolysis cell (MEC) to study the division of labor inside an anode-attached vertically stratified biofilm, where genetically modified Methanosarcina acetivorans and Escherichia coli perform the anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) to acetate followed by the aerobic conversion to 2,3-butanediol, respectively. We find that such a design is theoretically feasible, and we identify minimum biological improvements and operational conditions so that the aerobic layer effectively acts as oxygen-consuming living membrane protecting the anaerobic layer. Considering current biotechnological parameters points to a significant yet feasible need for further microbial engineering to increase the AOM rate. A comparison to a more traditional two-stage reactor at equivalent biomass reveals advantages and drawbacks of both designs, e.g., tradeoffs between peak product yield, reactor volume, and operational complexity. These results inform AOM driven microbial upgrading via aerobic-anaerobic stratified biofilms as well as value-added production via cooperative consortia in general.

papers.title: Noninvasive Cardiac Arrest Recognition Using Wearable Sensors in a Porcine Model of Ventricular Fibrillation
papers.abstract: Background: Wearable detection of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) could improve survival, given the prognostic importance of time to resuscitation and that 50% to 75% of events are unwitnessed. Existing systems may be limited by their form factor and by specificity achieved at the cost of sensitivity. We investigated whether the raw photoplethysmography (PPG) signal from low-cost wearable sensors contains a distinct signature of circulatory arrest. Methods: Ventricular fibrillation (VF) was electrically induced in 9 invasively monitored pigs while raw PPG was recorded with a wearable-class sensor. PPG dynamics after VF onset were related to aortic and right atrial pressures. A heuristic detection algorithm was evaluated for sensitivity and latency by leave-one-out cross-validation in the porcine data and for false positives in 57,857 hours of free-living PPG from 115 human participants. Results: After VF onset, the raw PPG showed a reproducible exponential decay (time constant 10.53 s; coefficient of variation 8.9% to 17.0% over the first 10 s) that tracked rising right atrial pressure (r = 0.90), reflecting arterial-to-venous blood redistribution. The algorithm detected VF in 8 of 9 animals (sensitivity 0.889; 95% CI, 0.518-0.997) with a median latency of 57.2 s. In the human cohort, it produced 2.73 false positives per user-year (95% CI, 1.62-4.31), comparable to current systems. Conclusions: Raw wearable PPG encodes circulatory collapse during VF, as supported by invasive hemodynamic measurements. While preliminary, these results suggest the potential for wearable-based OHCA detection with improved sensitivity, reduced latency, and comparable specificity.

papers.title: Profiling host-pathogen dynamic in a 3D human epidermal infection model and real-time sensing of IL-1α as a tissue-damage biomarker
papers.abstract: Skin infections begin with superficial colonization and progress to host tissue damage, yet the models used to study this process and the sensors intended to monitor it are rarely developed together. Here we combine a standardized three-dimensional human epidermal equivalent (HEE) infection model with an electrochemical immunosensor. By using a surface-restricted inoculation method, this model supported live pathogenic bacterial exposure on intact epidermis for up to seven days without bacterial contamination of the basolateral culture medium. Over the 7-day course, while commensal Staphylococcus epidermidis remained confined to the stratum corneum with preserved tissue integrity, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) caused progressive epidermal barrier damage and an inflammatory signaling cascade. Longitudinal cytokine profiling revealed distinct host-response profiles, identifying interleukin-1 (IL-1) as the most consistent and responsive indicator of the transition from colonization to active infection across both P. aeruginosa and MRSA groups. A laser-patterned gold/polyimide electrode functionalized with anti-IL-1 antibodies resolved the rise in IL-1 from bacterial colonization (day 4) to severe infection (day 7) by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, providing state discrimination rather than quantitative equivalence with ELISA. Overall, this integrated approach establishes a robust, animal-free platform that links infection-driven epidermal damage with biomarker-based electrochemical detection, providing a foundation for the development of next-generation in vitro diagnostics.

papers.title: Affibody-conjugated hyaluronic acid hydrogels within collagen sponges enhance dose-dependent BMP-2-mediated bone formation and repair of critically sized femoral defects
papers.abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) is a potent osteoinductive growth factor; however, its burst release from clinical collagen sponge carriers can cause inflammation and ectopic bone formation. Alternative delivery vehicles slow BMP-2 protein release through increased crosslinking density, which stiffens the polymer network and can restrict cell infiltration required for bone formation. Here, we introduce a BMP-2 delivery system in which a hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogel containing BMP-2-specific affibodies is formed within clinically used collagen sponges to retain BMP-2 through protein-material affinity interactions rather than physical entrapment. We developed a maleimide functionalized, hydrazone crosslinked HA hydrogel such that affibody conjugation is chemically orthogonal to network formation, allowing affibody density to be varied independently of crosslinking density. Forming this hydrogel within a collagen sponge produced composite scaffolds with improved surgical handling and BMP-2 retention. Moreover, in vitro, composite scaffolds exhibited minimal swelling while retaining more BMP-2 than the collagen sponge alone. In vivo, composite scaffolds conjugated with BMP-2-specific affibodies improved ectopic mineralization in a BMP-2 dose-dependent manner. In a critically sized femoral defect, composite scaffolds with and without affibodies significantly increased bone volume relative to the collagen sponge. Thus, this composite scaffold effectively integrates the clinically used collagen sponge with a tunable HA hydrogel and BMP-2-specific affibodies to improve BMP-2-mediated bone regeneration and expand the use of naturally derived biomaterials for bone healing.

papers.title: High-Throughput Coded Aperture Raman Imaging with Total Internal Reflection
papers.abstract: Spontaneous Raman microscopy provides label-free molecular fingerprints of biological tissues, but its low scattering efficiency limits the throughput required for large-area hyperspectral imaging. Here we introduce total internal reflection Raman (TIRR) microscopy, an architecture that exploits repeated internal reflections within a thin sapphire substrate to generate extended evanescent excitation without dividing the incident laser power among independent illumination spots. Combined with programmable Hadamard-coded detection, TIRR recovers spatially resolved Raman spectra with an effective spatial resolution of approximately 3.5 um and a spectral linewidth of approximately 10 cm-1. Hyperspectral imaging of human skin and colon tissues reveals heterogeneous Raman contrast across submillimeter-scale fields of view. Compared with confocal Raman microscopy, TIRR achieves a directly measured 9.0-fold reduction in acquisition time at lower excitation power, corresponding to a 20.1-fold power- and signal-to-noise-normalized acquisition-efficiency advantage. We further demonstrate compressive reconstruction using low-sequency Hadamard patterns, preserving high spectral and spatial fidelity in both the development dataset and an independent tissue specimen. This approach provides an additional nominal 2.1-fold acceleration, suggesting a potential combined normalized throughput enhancement approaching 40-fold. Finally, co-registration with spatial p21 annotations in a human skin section reveals exploratory Raman spectral differences associated with cellular senescence. TIRR thus establishes a programmable approach to accelerated spontaneous Raman imaging while retaining the multidimensional spectral information needed for molecular tissue analysis.

papers.title: Bioresorbable permanent-magnet beacons for tracking internal biomechanics during free movement
papers.abstract: Perioperative complications represent a global health burden that can be reduced through timely interventions guided by continuous physiological monitoring. Bioresorbable sensors excel through natural degradation without subsequent surgical extraction, but motion artefacts disrupt their accurate measurement. We synthesize bioresorbable permanent-magnet nanocomposites from aligned iron nanowires as implantable beacons. These beacons intrinsically generate magnetic fields responsive to biomechanical changes, thereby enabling wireless and chipless monitoring. An artificial-intelligence-enhanced wearable magnetic-field camera decodes these spatial maps into calibrated values that tolerate vigorous movement. The system achieves a displacement-equivalent mean absolute error of 2.74 m. Experiments in rat models demonstrate intracranial pressure tracking with clinical-grade accuracy during vigorous activities, and longitudinal monitoring of intracranial hypertension associated with ischaemic stroke during natural behaviours.

papers.title: Scaffold-Mediated Cellular and Acellular Delivery of Inducible BMP2-Lentivirus Promotes Atrophic Nonunion Fracture Healing without Heterotopic Ossification
papers.abstract: Nonunions occur in 5-10% of fracture patients, and current treatments are expensive with variable success. Controllable, localized delivery of BMP2 using porous, degradable scaffolds may be a promising alternative. We designed tube-shaped cryogel scaffolds (chitosan-gelatin, CG; chitosan-agarose-gelatin, CAG) to deliver a doxycycline-inducible BMP2-lentivirus vector (BMP2-LV). Results showed that CAG scaffolds have larger pores, higher toughness, and better cell infiltration than CG scaffolds. When scaffolds were implanted subcutaneously in mice and treated with continuous doxycycline, x-ray radiographs and microCT showed mineralization in scaffolds seeded with adipose-derived stem cells (BMP2-LV-ASC) but not acellular scaffolds (BMP2-LV) 4-weeks after implantation. Scaffolds that were implanted at the site of an established femoral nonunion 4-weeks after fracture and treated with continuous doxycycline showed improved healing with CG/CAG BMP2-LV and BMP2-LV-ASC compared to scaffold-only controls. At 2-weeks post implantation, microCT and histology showed that BMP2-expressing scaffolds promoted increased callus mineralization relative to scaffold-only. At 8-weeks post implantation, microCT and histology showed near-complete bone bridging in BMP2-treated groups compared to still visible fracture lines in the scaffold-only groups. However, CG/CAG BMP2-LV-ASC groups also showed heterotopic ossification. Finally, we demonstrated that heterotopic ossification was eliminated at 8-weeks post implantation in CG BMP2-LV-ASC groups by restricting doxycycline treatment to the first 3 days after implantation. We conclude that lentiviral BMP2 delivery using cellularized and acellular cryogel scaffolds enhanced fracture healing in a nonunion model, and that a 3-day period of BMP2 induction using an inducible system was sufficient to promote healing without the complication of heterotopic ossification.

papers.title: Dual photoresponsive hydrogel surfaces enabling integrated single-cell analysis of morphology and gene expression
papers.abstract: Integrated single-cell analysis linking time-resolved cellular phenotypic dynamics with gene expression is essential for understanding cellular heterogeneity but remains technically challenging. Here, we report a dual photoresponsive hydrogel that combines a photoactivatable cell-trapping material with a photodegradable hydrogel, enabling light-directed single-cell capture, time-resolved imaging, and the on-demand release of selected cells for downstream gene expression analysis. This approach allows cells to be arrayed at a high density with uniform spacing, facilitating high-throughput monitoring of morphological dynamics. Cells exhibiting phenotypes of interest can be precisely retrieved by localized hydrogel degradation induced by secondary light irradiation and subsequently subjected to single-cell gene expression analysis. Using this workflow in combination with high-throughput real-time image processing technology, we directly link dynamic morphological features to gene expression and demonstrated the ability of the workflow to examine transcriptional alterations associated with invasive cancer cell behavior.

papers.title: Towards an understanding of injury in aortic tissue prior to actual failure: quantification of mechanically induced collagen damage using collagen hybridizing peptides
papers.abstract: The development, validation, and optimization of endovascular aortic devices require quantitative assessment of tissue damage occurring during surgical interventions. Until now, this assessment--before complete failure--has been largely unfeasible for lack of a suitable methodology. Recently developed collagen hybridizing peptides (CHPs) allow selective detection of damage to collagen, the primary load-bearing constituent of the aortic wall. However, their application in large, mechanically loaded arteries has not yet been established. Therefore, we optimized an experimental workflow for large arteries that accounts for their energy-storage function and geometrical constraints; furthermore, we have characterized the tissue's autofluorescence and selected a suitable CHP fluorophore. Specimens from a single porcine aorta were examined using uniaxial tensile testing, histological analysis, fluorescence spectral analysis, confocal microscopy, and quantitative image analysis to present collagen damage as a function of tissue stretch. The workflow detected load-induced collagen damage before tissue failure, whereas histological evaluation showed no obvious load-induced disruption. Damage scores were comparable between the undeformed control and the specimen stretched by a factor of 1.2, while specimens stretched beyond 1.2 exhibited elevated scores. This pattern corresponded to higher complication rates with excessive stent oversizing. Furthermore, the proposed protocol can be adapted for ex vivo stent deployment experiments to compare collagen damage resulting from various aortic device designs and deployment conditions. Quantitative damage metrics could inform structurally motivated constitutive material models for computational simulations of endovascular interventions. Combined with histological and structural analyses, this workflow could also help link tissue composition--or organization--to individual susceptibility to damage.

papers.title: Pseudo-Central Retinal Blood Vessel in Pig, Sheep and Goat
papers.abstract: Humans and non-human primates have central retinal blood vessels (CRBVs) through their optic nerve head (ONH). The collagen of pig, sheep and goat ONHs also forms structures that look like CRBVs. We aimed to determine whether the CRBV-like structures in pig, sheep and goat are true CRBVs or if they should instead be called pseudo-CRBVs. Coronal sections through the ONHs of human, monkey, pig, sheep and goat eyes were imaged for collagen. We then used DAPI, multicolor DiOlistics and GFAP immunostaining to visualize nuclei, astrocytes and other ONH constituents. CRBV-like structures were classified into three types: true CRBVs if the structure was only a blood vessel; fully pseudo-CRBV if the evidence indicated only neural tissues or cells other than erythrocytes within; or partial pseudo-CRBV if some of the region appeared as a vessel and other parts did not. All eyes exhibited CRBV-like structures in the collagen. In human and monkey eyes they were all true CRBVs. Conversely, the CRBV-like structures were fully or partially pseudo-CRBVs in 80% (4/5) of pig, 50% (3/6) of sheep and 100% (2/2) of goat eyes. In majority of pig, sheep and goat eyes, CRBV-like structures were actually pseudo-CRBVs. Often, what appeared like a vessel lumen, was instead filled by neural tissues reminiscent of pores. The mechanisms that lead to CRBV-like structures that are not actually CRBVs in these three species, but not in humans and monkeys, remain unknown.

papers.title: Monolith, porous bead, membrane or fibre? A comparative characterisation of four oligo-dT affinity chromatography matrices for mRNA capture
papers.abstract: Oligo-deoxythymidine (oligo dT) affinity chromatography is the most widely used capture step for in vitro transcribed mRNA and is now offered in four stationary-phase architectures, yet, to our knowledge, no published study has compared all four. We characterised a monolith, perfusive porous beads, a membrane adsorber and an electrospun cellulose fibre adsorber with a short (eGFP, 930 nt) and a long (SARS CoV 2 spike, S 2P, 4284 nt) mRNA. After screening the loading salt (NaCl or guanidine hydrochloride, Gu HCl), we mapped load flow rate, load concentration and Gu HCl concentration with response surface designs and compared the formats at near-optimal conditions. Gu HCl gave a higher peak recovery than NaCl in seven of the eight matrix construct combinations. At the near-optimal runs, the fibre adsorber recovered 17.9 mg eGFP and 13.3 mg S 2P per mL of bed, 2.3 to 2.6 fold the membrane and 3.5- to 4.8-fold the monolith and beads (p membrane > monolith > beads (0.314 to 0.035 mg/mL/min for eGFP). The membrane and fibre adsorber lost yield sharply above 0.4 to 0.6 M Gu HCl, whereas the monolith and beads declined gradually. In an amortised cost model at baseline cost inputs, the fibre adsorber was the least expensive format per milligram of purified mRNA at every number of device cycles (USD 114 to 140/mg for single use and 78 to 92/mg at 20 cycles), and the membrane the most expensive. A one at a time sensitivity analysis over wide ranges of the mRNA feed cost, the labour and facility rate, the device price and the number of cycles per device left the fibre adsorber the least expensive format in almost every combination examined, with the mRNA feed cost the dominant input. Only the monolith and beads are currently marketed as GMP grade, process scale materials, so the choice of format depends on whether capacity, productivity, cost or manufacturing readiness takes priority.

papers.title: Associations between structural and functional hemodynamics in the optic nerve head
papers.abstract: Purpose: Glaucoma is characterized by progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells axons thought to initiate within the optic nerve head (ONH). Although the precise mechanisms remain unclear, a leading hypothesis suggests that insufficient blood flow and oxygenation may be significant contributors to axonal damage. Measuring ONH oxygenation directly, however, is difficult. Hence, our first goal was to identify associations between structural and functional hemodynamics parameters (flow and oxygenation). We then evaluated whether local tissue oxygenation and hypoxia can be estimated from measurable parameters. Methods: Following previously reported methods, the ONH vasculature of four healthy monkey eyes was reconstructed. Numerical simulations were performed to determine blood flow and oxygen distribution. Structural parameters of each segment, including spatial location, orientation, length, and tortuosity, and functional hemodynamics parameters of each segment, including blood flow, pressure, blood oxygenation, and surrounding tissue oxygenation, were quantified. Results: Structural parameters exhibited no distinct spatial distribution, whereas hemodynamic and oxygenation parameters followed radial patterns. Although blood flow correlated with tissue oxygenation (p<0.001), regional mismatches indicated that flow alone was insufficient to predict accurately local oxygenation. We developed two multivariable mixed-effects models using measurable structural and flow parameters, a quadratic model that predicted continuous tissue oxygenation with high accuracy (R^2=0.75) and a logistic model that estimated local hypoxia risk. Conclusions: Our results provide a framework for estimating local tissue oxygenation and hypoxia risk that currently cannot be measured experimentally from vascular structural and flow parameters that can be measured.

papers.title: CT-Derived In Vitro Model Simulating Neonatal Cranial Growth
papers.abstract: Purpose: This study presents an in vitro platform for quantitatively simulating cranial growth in neonates from 3 to 6 months of age. Methods: The system integrates a pneumatic-hydraulic actuation unit, multi-camera optical tracking, and a CT-compatible enclosure to replicate and measure intracranial expansion. A phantom head model was fabricated via 3D printing using cranial bones and flexible latex sutures, reproducing neonatal cranial biomechanics. Controlled hydraulic pressure simulates intracranial volume (ICV) growth, while surface and volumetric changes are captured through synchronized imaging. Results: Morphometric parameters - biparietal diameter, occipitofrontal diameter, cranial circumference, and ICV - were measured and compared against published reference data. The system achieved high reproducibility across repeated trials. CT-derived ICV values (R2 = 0.98) closely matched reference trends, with average manufacturing deviations of 0-4 mm between fabricated and reference geometries. Linear morphometric increments confirmed physiologically consistent expansion patterns. Conclusion: The proposed platform provides a quantitatively validated, controllable, and CT-compatible environment for studying neonatal cranial development. It enables biomechanical testing and device evaluation under ethical and repeatable in vitro conditions, with potential future applications in surgical training and pre-operative planning.

papers.title: Membrane Biofouling and Plasmid Conformation Shape the Retention of Antibiotic Resistance Gene-Carrying Plasmids during Ultrafiltration
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a growing threat to human and environmental health, and wastewater treatment plants are important pathways for the release of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Although ultrafiltration (UF) membranes effectively retain antibiotic-resistant bacteria, their capacity to remove extracellular ARGs remains less understood. Extracellular plasmids are concerning because they persist following cell lysis and may contribute to horizontal gene transfer. Unlike intact bacterial cells, these flexible DNA molecules may pass through membrane barriers. Here, we investigated the removal of extracellular plasmids carrying ARGs using a 100 kDa molecular weight cut-off (MWCO) UF membrane, focusing on biofouling, plasmid size, and conformation. Initial filtration experiments achieved removal efficiency (RE) above 99.9% for antibiotic-resistant bacteria and plasmids, and produced a pronounced biofouling layer. For the pre-fouled membrane, mass balances showed increased adsorption and permeation of plasmids, with RE declining from approximately 99% to below 95% over consecutive runs. Microscopy indicated plasmid deposition in biofouled regions. Additionally, plasmid size showed no consistent relationship with RE, while conformation had a pronounced effect, with supercoiled plasmids being retained more efficiently (98.8-99.6%) than their linear counterparts (82.4-92.4%). These findings demonstrate that plasmid retention by UF is influenced by both membrane conditions and DNA conformation, which nominal membrane pore size alone cannot capture. The high RE highlights the potential of UF as a tertiary treatment, while emphasizing the need to account for biofouling and DNA structural diversity when evaluating strategies to reduce extracellular ARG discharge from wastewater treatment plants.

papers.title: Force Volume Atomic Force Microscopy of THP-1 and Primary Mouse Macrophages Reveals that the Mechanical Signature of Macrophage Polarization is Model-Dependent
papers.abstract: Macrophages are immune cells with a rich morphological variety and markedly different biological functions when differentiated into M0 (non-activated) macrophages or polarized into M1 (pro-inflammatory) and M2 (anti-inflammatory) phenotypes. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) studies have recently associated a mechanical dimension with macrophage polarization. Herein, the elastic properties of the three phenotypes are measured and compared by force volume AFM in two less explored models: THP-1-derived macrophages (cell line) and mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs, primary cells). High-indentation measurements (indentation higher than 2 micrometers) with colloidal probes capture the full cell deformation, and a recently derived spherical model with bottom effect correction provides quantitative values of the Youngs modulus (E) that account for substrate effects and cell height with the correct probe geometry. THP-1-derived macrophages show significant mechanical differences, with EM1 higher than EM2 and EM0, whereas BMDMs show no significant differences between phenotypes. Furthermore, BMDM-derived M0 and M2 macrophages show 1.5 to 2 times higher E than the corresponding THP-1 phenotypes. The elasticity of cells with different shapes is also evaluated to account for the heterogeneous macrophage morphology found in all samples. These results indicate that the mechanical signature of macrophage polarization is model-dependent.
